findings.reason: The protected Python solution finds the most similar graph path to a target path using dynamic programming across target path layers. For each position 0 to m-1 and ending city, it finds the optimal predecessor city among graph neighbors that minimizes total name mismatches, storing parent pointers for backtracking. The solution runs in O(m * (n + e)) time and O(m * n + e) space; no candidate is required.

Layered DP guarantees that every valid graph walk of length m is evaluated, and choosing the minimum cost neighbor for each step finds a path with global minimum edit distance. Backtracking via parent pointers reconstructs a valid path.

Scanning all neighbors across m layers takes O(m * (n + e)) time. Predecessor table of size m x n and graph adjacency list take O(m * n + e) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts n, roads, names, and targetPath, returning a list of m city indices representing a valid graph walk with minimum edit distance.

The approach accurately details target position DP layering, neighbor transition optimization, predecessor backtracking, and O(m * (n + e)) time / O(m * n + e) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover exponential graph walk enumeration, dense predecessor scan overhead, layered graph shortest-path equivalence, one-name targets, city/road revisiting, repeated names, greedy trap avoidance, and judge acceptance of any optimal route.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical layered graph DP algorithm with SHA-256 digests 4290f8071001921373103668116b6102b8a6294ce2a6cb1c08d10d08ea80ef8d and 200a5e6affb303f01931714b13f9e04dc6b078968f18f7f209492f530c51d04b. Verified submission remains untouched.
